notes: Prompts 1-10 are the required scenarios; 11-14 cover preservation, genre styling and DAW safety. 'objective' assertions can be graded from the transcript or checked with scripts/mc.py; 'subjective' ones need a human listening pass (import the generated MIDI and play it). Passing objective checks does not prove musical quality.

evals.name: jazzy-dnb-4-bar-progression
evals.prompt: Write a dark, jazzy four-bar chord progression for a liquid drum and bass tune at 174. One chord per bar, Rhodes plus a sub bass.
evals.expected_output: Four extended-minor-leaning chords suited to liquid DnB, each with a rootless Rhodes voicing (names + octaves + MIDI) and a sub-bass note, short why-it-works, offer to write MIDI/clip.

assertions.text: Gives exactly four chords, one per bar
Every chord has a voicing with note names AND MIDI numbers
Every voicing's notes belong to its stated chord and include its 3rd and 7th (verify with mc.py check)
Keys voicings sit at or above MIDI 48 and the bass notes are in the sub range (MIDI 24-43)
States the octave convention (C3 = 60) once
Explanation is brief (no unrequested theory lecture)
Sounds dark and jazzy and fits liquid DnB when played back

evals.name: rhodes-voicings
evals.prompt: I've got Dm9 G13 Cmaj9 A7b13. Give me practical Rhodes voicings I can actually play, there's a bassline already.
evals.expected_output: Rootless one-hand (or clearly split) Rhodes voicings with smooth voice leading, MIDI numbers, and hand-split info.

assertions.text: Voicings are rootless or explain why the root is included
Each voicing has 3-5 notes and spans 12 semitones or less, or says how to split it between hands
All voicings validate against their chord symbols
Adjacent voicings share or step-move notes (reports held notes / movement)
Lowest voicing note is at or above MIDI 50

evals.name: harmonize-bassline
evals.prompt: What chords work with my bassline? It's F1 for three beats then A1 on beat 4, Bb1 for three beats then E1, Eb1 for a whole bar, Ab1 for a whole bar. Loops every 4 bars. Ableton octave names.
evals.expected_output: Recognises A1 and E1 as approach notes, harmonises the downbeats (F, Bb, Eb, Ab), offers 2-3 options with different intents, voiced and validated against the bass.

assertions.text: Treats A1 and E1 as approach/passing notes rather than harmonising them as chord roots
Each option's chords contain the downbeat bass note (as root or a named inversion/colour)
Offers 2-3 options whose musical intents differ and are named
Provides voicings with MIDI numbers for at least the recommended option
Does not change the user's bassline

evals.name: identify-from-midi
evals.expected_output: Fm9, Bbm9, Eb13, Abmaj9 (lowest notes as bass), with notes/degrees and the key context (F minor / Ab major).

assertions.text: Names bar 1 as Fm9
Names bar 2 as Bbm9
Names bar 3 as Eb13
Names bar 4 as Abmaj9
Mentions the key is F minor / Ab major (or notes the ambiguity)

evals.name: three-reharmonizations
evals.prompt: Give me three alternative ways to reharmonise Cmaj7 Am7 Dm7 G7. The top melody notes are G, C, F, F (one per bar) and must stay.
evals.expected_output: Three options with distinct intents (e.g. richer diatonic, functional/tritone, borrowed/darker), each keeping the melody notes compatible, voiced and explained briefly.

assertions.text: Exactly three options, each labelled with its intent or technique
The three options differ in technique, not just in added extensions
In every option each melody note is a chord tone or available tension of its chord (mc.py validate --role melody shows no flags)
Voicings keep the melody note as the top voice
At least one option keeps bar 1 as some form of C major chord

evals.name: explain-to-non-theory-person
evals.prompt: Why does Cmaj7 to Fm7 back to Cmaj7 sound so bittersweet? I don't know theory, explain it simply.
evals.expected_output: Plain-language explanation: Fm7 is borrowed from C minor; A and E drop to Ab and Eb; the semitone drop creates the sigh; names modal interchange after the explanation.

assertions.text: Names the specific notes that change (A to Ab, and the Eb)
Describes the effect in sound terms before or alongside the theory term
Any jargon used (modal interchange, borrowed chord, parallel minor) is defined in plain words
Gives the actual notes or MIDI numbers so the user can try it
Length is proportionate (not a full lesson)

evals.name: melody-over-harmony
evals.prompt: Write a 4-bar melody for a Rhodes or flute over Fm9 Bbm9 Eb13 Abmaj9 (one bar each) at 172. Something singable with a motif.
evals.expected_output: A motif-based melody with rhythm in beats, note names + MIDI, strong beats on chord tones/tensions, validated, one-line description of its shape.

assertions.text: Melody given as a note list with start times/durations in beats and MIDI numbers
Has an identifiable motif that is repeated or varied (not a random scale walk)
At least 70% of strong-beat notes are chord tones or tensions (mc.py validate --role melody)
Range is within about an octave and a half
Is singable and fits the chords when played

evals.name: midi-compatible-output
evals.prompt: Give me Cm9 Fm9 Abmaj7 G7alt as pad chords, two bars each, in a format I can paste into a MIDI tool or drop into Ableton.
evals.expected_output: Note list with pitch/start_time/duration/velocity in beats (and/or .mid files), verified, 32 beats total.

assertions.text: Provides structured note data (pitch, start time, duration, velocity) or .mid file(s)
All pitches are integers 0-127 and durations are positive
Chords start at beats 0, 8, 16, 24 and last 8 beats
Each chord's pitches validate against its symbol
States the octave/pitch convention

evals.name: ambiguous-harmony
evals.prompt: My chord stab is Ab C Eb G. Is that Abmaj7 or something else? The bass is moving underneath.
evals.expected_output: Explains it is Abmaj7 or a rootless Fm9 (also C-based readings possible) depending on the bass; shows what each bass note does.

assertions.text: Mentions both Abmaj7 and Fm9 (rootless) readings
Explains that the bass note decides which one is heard
Does not assert a single answer as definitive

evals.name: no-mcp-installed
evals.prompt: Write me a deep house m9 stab loop in A minor and put it straight into Ableton.
evals.expected_output: With no Ableton MCP available: one-line limitation, then .mid file(s) and the note table; does not claim to have written to Live.

assertions.text: Checks for an Ableton MCP and states plainly that none is available
Delivers the idea as .mid file(s) and/or a note table instead
Does not claim to have written anything into Ableton
The stab voicings validate and use a short-note rhythm

evals.name: preserve-user-intent
evals.prompt: From Fm9 Bbm9 Eb13 Abmaj9: I like the first two chords, but not the last two. Give me alternatives for bars 3 and 4.
evals.expected_output: Bars 1-2 unchanged (same voicings); 2-3 alternatives for bars 3-4 with different intents.

assertions.text: Bars 1 and 2 keep the same chords and the same voicings as before
Offers alternatives for bars 3-4 only
Alternatives are voice-led from bar 2 and back into bar 1 (loop)

evals.name: late-90s-atmospheric
evals.prompt: Make Am7 Dm7 G7 Cmaj7 sound more like late-90s atmospheric drum and bass.
evals.expected_output: Moves away from the functional ii-V feel toward m9/maj9 planing, lydian colour, pedal points, slower harmonic rhythm, pads; explains briefly.

assertions.text: Uses at least one of: planing/constant structure, lydian maj7#11, sus chords, pedal point, slower harmonic rhythm
Gives pad/Rhodes voicings with MIDI numbers
Explains the change in one or two lines of sound-terms

evals.name: mcp-no-overwrite
evals.prompt: [With an Ableton MCP connected and an existing chord clip on track 2, slot 1] Make a more soulful variation of the chords on track 2.
evals.expected_output: Reads the clip, analyses it, writes the variation to a NEW empty slot, names it, verifies by reading back; original untouched.

assertions.text: Reads the existing clip's notes before proposing changes
Writes to an empty slot or new track, never the original clip
Names the new clip and tells the user where it is
Reads the new clip back and validates it
Does not use the server's generator tools to replace musical decisions

evals.name: simplicity-when-appropriate
evals.prompt: The chords in my neurofunk drop are clashing with the reese. Fm11 Gbmaj9#11 Ebm11 Dbmaj9. Help.
evals.expected_output: Recommends simplifying (shells/triads/fewer notes, higher register, slower changes) rather than adding complexity; verified voicings.

assertions.text: Recommends reducing density or extensions and/or moving the voicings up
Does not add more extensions
Gives concrete voicings with MIDI numbers above the bass register
